context: Set 1 of 3 — the four blocks that gate the most work in the glpnet lane. Marathon run mrun-20d9230f767b, feature 078-verification-receipts. Every figure quoted was measured this session; the full brief with evidence tables is at claude.ai/code/artifact/77dcfcf1.

questions.question: Work reaches a host only when someone writes an addressed `allocate --to <actor>`. Measured on D:/coop/glpnet/sched: 22 of 32 packets are engineer_id='unassigned', ZERO are ready-and-unallocated, and the allocator's own host has 59 ops and ZERO availability windows since 2026-08-13. Three lanes now report 'compliant and idle'. The fleet spent today raising WORKER availability while the supply half stayed shut. How do you want the supply half opened?
blocks: any use of the 35-day calendars just declared

options.label: Direct ariellas, with a deadline
options.means: ariellas declares a calendar on the allocator host and issues addressed allocations, against a named date. Two commands on one host; no code.
options.cost: Does not explain why the gap persisted 11 days, and leaves the fleet on a single allocator who has been unreachable all day.

options.label: Move allocation authority
options.means: Transfer allocation authority to any lane that is present and can write it, ending the single-allocator dependency.
options.cost: Reverses a deliberate centralisation. Two allocators can address the same packet, and allocation uniqueness is not enforced anywhere.

options.label: Lanes self-allocate under policy
options.means: Each lane draws from the reserved pool under a declared, recorded policy.
options.cost: Highest duplicate risk: cross-root duplicate allocation is ALREADY observed at 8.4%, and the host dimension is not recorded at all. This would raise it.

questions.question: codexreview is now unblocked and it RAN on 078: exit 0, 10 findings, 8 HIGH — every one a way the receipts module can pass without proving it ran, which is the exact defect 078 exists to eliminate. Two are test defects: a conformance fixture that reports full coverage without exercising its declared BOUNDED case, and a mutation test that stays GREEN under a no-op validator. 99 commits sit unreleased behind this. How do you want it sequenced?

options.label: Fix tests first, then product
options.means: Fix the two test findings as a first slice, then the six product HIGHs, then re-review and release. Instruments before readings.
options.cost: The 99-commit release waits for two slices rather than one. Roughly mini plus midi of work before any ship.

options.label: Fix all ten, then release
options.means: One implementation slice covering all 10 findings; single re-review; single release.
options.cost: The six product fixes would be certified by a suite whose own guards are still unproven, so their green run means less than it appears to.

options.label: Release now, fix 078 after
options.means: Cut the release excluding codeconv/receipts, then remediate 078 on a follow-up.
options.cost: 078's code is already on develop, so excluding it is a revert, not an omission. Reverting to ship around a defect is how the defective onrestart script shipped on 08-21.

questions.question: 078's tasks.md holds 66 tasks and 54 of them are prefixed `bk:` — they name work in the buildkit repo, not glpnet. /bk-implement 078 has been blocked on this since 2026-08-20, and it now also gates the buildkit-side fix for the git-pathspec defect I root-caused today. 078 is WSJF rank 1 and gates five other features. How may this lane execute buildkit-repo tasks?

options.label: Branch and PR in buildkit
options.means: This lane may branch and open PRs in the buildkit repo for tasks its own feature owns, under a naming convention like glpnet/<feature>-<topic> so cross-repo branches stay attributable.
options.cost: Two lanes then commit into buildkit concurrently; the buildkit repo already sits on another session's branch with uncommitted work, so collisions are real.

options.label: Hand tasks to buildkit lane
options.means: The 54 bk: tasks become a dependency owned by the buildkit lane; 078 waits for them.
options.cost: 078 has already waited four days on this question and would then wait indefinitely on another lane's queue, while holding the single active slot.

options.label: Re-scope 078 to glpnet only
options.means: 078 keeps its 12 glpnet tasks; the 54 become a separate buildkit feature with its own roadmap row.
options.cost: Splits a coherent feature across two roadmaps and two WSJF scores, and splits the verification thesis whose whole point is being end-to-end.

questions.question: Two branches implement overlapping full-Gleam work and cannot both survive: origin/050-full-gleam-combined is 48 commits ahead with 21 conflicts, origin/059-full-scope-gleam-glp-implementation is 32 ahead with 30 conflicts across 248 files. Your 2026-08-21 ruling triaged the other post-PR lines but left this one as the engineer's call, and it has been open three days. Which line survives?
blocks: 2 of the 5 remaining unmerged origin heads

options.label: 059 survives, archive 050
options.means: Archive-tag 050 and drop it; merge 059. Chosen on the one differentiator anyone has measured — an earlier sweep found 059 the only line with real substance.
options.cost: That evidence is thin: a single prior finding, not a content comparison. I have NOT diffed the two implementations against each other.

options.label: 050 survives, archive 059
options.means: Archive-tag 059 and drop it; merge 050 — the larger commit count and the lighter conflict load.
options.cost: Discards the line previously found to carry measured substance, on the basis of conflict count rather than content.

options.label: Measure both before ruling
options.means: I diff the two implementations against each other and bring you a content comparison, replacing a judgement call with a measurement.
options.cost: Delays the ruling by a bounded piece of work, and keeps two unmerged heads alive meanwhile.
